sources.citation: National Highways (2022). CD 122 Geometric design of grade separated junctions (formerly TD 22/06, TD 39/94, TD 40/94), Version 1.1.1, published 31 Jan 2022. Design Manual for Roads and Bridges, Road Layout Design.
sources.how_read: Downloaded the PDF (4.56 MB, watermark 'CD 122 Version 1.1.1, published: 31-Jan-2022') and converted it with pdftotext. Read all of 'Terms and definitions' (pp. 7-9) and Section 3 on merges, 3.1 to 3.25 (pp. 12-22). Figure 3.14c (p. 18) and Table 3.21 (p. 21) were checked on rendered page images, because the figures are drawings. Also read the merge clauses of the England National Application Annex in the same PDF (E/1.3, E/2.3-E/2.5, E/3.3-E/3.4). Not read: the diverge clauses, Sections 4-5, and CD 109 (the design-speed standard it refers to).
sources.length_definition: Layout B, the parallel merge (Figure 3.14c), runs nose, then auxiliary lane, then auxiliary-lane taper ending at the entry datum ('end of downstream taper', Table 3.5). The auxiliary lane runs from the downstream tip of the nose to the start of the taper. The nose and the taper are separate columns in Table 3.21 and are not part of the auxiliary-lane length. NOTE 3: lengths are measured along the projected nearside edge of the mainline carriageway. Definition: 'Parallel merge/diverge: a merge or diverge layout where an auxiliary lane is provided alongside the mainline carriageway'.
sources.design_speed: The rural motorway rows (Mainline; Within Interchange) are not indexed by design speed. The rural all-purpose rows are '120 kph' and '100A kph or less'. 'A' is printed as shown; it is probably the CD 109 design-speed band suffix [VERIFY against CD 109]. The plant sets a 100 km/h limit, not a design speed, so the matching row is ambiguous: motorway (type of road) or 100A all-purpose (speed).
sources.guidance_range_m: Rural motorway mainline: auxiliary lane at least 230 m, plus a 75 m taper (nose 115 m). §3.21.1: extend to 370 m or more where merge and mainline flows both reach at least 85 % of design capacity for more than 1,000 h/yr. Rural all-purpose 100A kph or less: at least 160 m plus a 55 m taper. Rural all-purpose 120 kph: at least 190 m plus 55 m. §3.21.2: extend on uphill grades above 2 % with more than 10 % HGVs.
sources.location_in_source: Terms and definitions pp. 7-9; Table 3.5 p. 14; §3.14 Figure 3.14c 'Layout B - parallel merge' p. 18; Table 3.21 'Merge layouts geometric parameters' p. 21; NOTE 3 and §3.21.1-3.21.2 p. 22
sources.verbatim_extract: Table 3.21, columns: entry taper | min nose ratio | nose length | minimum auxiliary lane length | length of auxiliary lane taper | ghost island tail (metres). 'Rural motorway / Mainline 205 1:40 115 230 75 180'; 'Rural all-purpose design speed / 100A kph or less 130 1:25 75 160 55 150'. NOTE 3: 'The merge layout lengths are measured along the projected nearside edge of the mainline carriageway, with the exception of the overlap, reduction taper and the 50 metres and 3.75V separations ...'. 3.21.1: 'On rural motorway mainlines, auxiliary lane lengths should be extended to 370 metres or greater where merge and mainline traffic flows are both forecast to reach or exceed 85% of the maximum design capacities given in Figure 3.12b for more than 1,000 hours per year.'
sources.note: 'Inside' here means: above the 230 m motorway minimum (and above the 160 m all-purpose 100A minimum), but below the 370 m extended length for high-flow merges. Every CD 122 parallel layout also has a taper (75 m on motorways). The plant has none: its 295 m is at full width up to an abrupt lane end. Measured from the nose tip to the end of the taper, the motorway minimum is 230 + 75 = 305 m, so the plant is 10 m shorter to the lane end. Whether the plant's flows meet the 85 %-of-capacity condition was not checked.

sources.citation: Texas Department of Transportation. Roadway Design Manual (online): Section 15.7.7 'Ramp Terminal Design' with Figure 15-25, and Section 4.10.2.3 'Acceleration Lanes' with Table 4-18 'Minimum Acceleration Lane Lengths for Entrance Terminals with Flat Grades of Less Than 3 percent'. sources.how_read: Fetched both HTML pages with curl and stripped the markup. Read all of Section 15.7.7 (15.7.7.1 to 15.7.7.9) and all of 4.10.2.3 with Tables 4-18 and 4-19. sources.length_definition: La (Table 4-18) is 'Measured Along Ramp Alignment' from Point A, the feature that controls speed on the ramp, to the beginning of the downstream taper. Lg (gap acceptance) is 'Measured Along Main Lane Alignment' from where the traveled ways are at least 2 ft apart to the start of the taper. For the parallel type: 'measured from the point where the left edge of the ramp travel way joins the traveled way of the freeway to the beginning of the downstream taper, Lg'. The taper (at least 300 ft) is excluded ('The taper section is not included in the length of the SCL'). Use La or Lg, whichever is greater.
sources.design_speed: Rows are highway design speed in mph; 60 mph (96.6 km/h) and 65 mph (104.6 km/h) bracket 100 km/h. Columns are the design speed of the controlling feature on the ramp, from stop condition to 50 mph. Conversions to metres are mine (1 ft = 0.3048 m).
sources.guidance_range_m: La at 60 mph: 1,200 ft (365.8 m) from a stop, falling to 180 ft (54.9 m) at a 50 mph ramp speed; 910 ft (277.4 m) at 30 mph, 1,020 ft (310.9 m) at 25 mph. La at 65 mph: 1,410 ft (429.8 m) from a stop, 370 ft (112.8 m) at 50 mph; 770 ft (234.7 m) at 40 mph, 1,000 ft (304.8 m) at 35 mph. Lg minimum 300 ft (91.4 m), or 300-500 ft (91-152 m) depending on nose width. Taper at least 300 ft (91.4 m). Desirable La of at least 1,200 ft (365.8 m) plus taper where the ramp-freeway volume nears 4,600 veh/h.
sources.location_in_source: RDM 15.7.7.1 and 15.7.7.3 (text and Figure 15-25); RDM 4.10.2.3 and Table 4-18
sources.verbatim_extract: 15.7.7.3: 'A minimum taper length of 300-ft is required. The length of a parallel-type acceleration lane is generally measured from the point where the left edge of the ramp travel way joins the traveled way of the freeway to the beginning of the downstream taper, Lg.' ... 'An acceleration length, La, of at least 1,200-ft plus the taper is desirable where the ramp-freeway volume is nearing 4,600 vehicles per hour at the ramp-freeway junction.' 15.7.7.1: 'The minimum gap acceptance length is 300-ft.' Table 4-18 rows (ft; stop, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50 mph): '60 | 1200 1140 1100 1020 910 800 550 420 180'; '65 | 1410 1350 1310 1220 1120 1000 770 600 370'.
sources.note: 295 m lies inside the 55-430 m span of La at 60-65 mph, and the reading depends on the ramp speed at Point A. It is above La for ramp controlling speeds of at least 30 mph (60 mph row) or at least 40 mph (65 mph row), and above the 91-152 m Lg. It is below La from a stop (366-430 m) and below the 366 m desirable high-volume length. The plant has no end taper; TxDOT requires at least 300 ft (91 m). The plant ramp is straight with a 100 km/h limit, so under TxDOT's rule part of the ramp could count toward La. If ramp vehicles stop at the ramp signal, the stop line is about 38 m upstream of lane 3a_0 (rj_0 28.33 m plus internal lane 9.82 m), giving roughly 333 m. I believe Table 4-18 reproduces the AASHTO Green Book table (US customary), but TxDOT does not attribute it on this page and I did not confirm it [VERIFY].

sources.length_definition: Metered entrances use an auxiliary lane measured 'downstream of the gore point' (504.3(2)(a)) or 'beyond the ramp convergence point' (504.3(2)(c)). In Figure 504.3C, the '300' Min.' dimension runs from the convergence point to the start of the 600 ft 50:1 taper, so the taper is excluded. The standard non-metered entrance (Figure 504.2A) is a taper-type design, not a parallel lane. Its 'acceleration lane length' runs from the inlet nose (14-ft point) to the 12-ft point: 167.11 ft + 300 ft = 467.11 ft (142.4 m). A 600 ft (182.9 m) 50:1 convergence follows (504.2(3)).
sources.design_speed: Not indexed by design speed. 504.2(4)(b): the inlet-nose design speed should be at least 50 mph for high-standard approaches. Conversions to metres are mine.
sources.guidance_range_m: Metered entrance auxiliary lane: at least 300 ft (91.4 m). At least 1,000 ft (304.8 m) when ramp volume exceeds 1,500 veh/h, or where trucks (3+ axles) are at least 5 % on sustained upgrades above 3 %. At least 500 ft (152.4 m) for trucks on grades under restrictive conditions (Figure 504.3C note 4). Each is followed by a 600 ft (182.9 m) 50:1 taper. 504.2(5)(b): 1,500 ft (457.2 m) on ascending ramps with more than 20 trucks/h and upgrades above 2 %.
sources.location_in_source: Index 504.2(3), p. 500-12; Figure 504.2A, p. 500-13; Index 504.3(2)(a), p. 500-18; Figure 504.3C, p. 500-22; Index 504.3(2)(c) (metered multilane text)
sources.verbatim_extract: 504.3(2)(a): 'Due to the operational benefits of an auxiliary lane, metered single or multilane freeway entrance ramps should include an auxiliary lane with a minimum length of 300 feet downstream of the gore point.' ... 'When vehicle volume exceeds 1500 vph, a 1,000 - foot minimum length of auxiliary lane should be provided downstream of the gore point for metered single or multilane freeway entrance ramps and connectors.' 504.3(2)(c): 'The merge from the metered entrance ramp to the freeway should include a 300-foot minimum auxiliary lane beyond the ramp convergence point.' 504.2(3): 'On entrance ramps the distance from the inlet nose (14-foot point) to the end of the acceleration lane taper should equal the sum of the distances shown on Figure 504.2A.'
sources.note: 295 m is above the 91.4 m minimum for a metered auxiliary lane and about 10 m below the 304.8 m minimum when ramp volume exceeds 1,500 veh/h. Caltrans adds a 600 ft (183 m) 50:1 taper, which the plant lacks. I did not compute the plant's ramp volumes against the 1,500 veh/h threshold. This source was not among the plan's candidates; see deviations.

read.deviations:
1. AASHTO Green Book (a plan candidate) was not read: it is paywalled and I found no legitimate full text. US guidance comes from two state manuals instead. TxDOT RDM Table 4-18 is, I believe, the Green Book's acceleration-length table in US customary units, but TxDOT does not say so on the page and I did not confirm it. Any AASHTO figure stays [VERIFY].
2. Caltrans HDM Chapter 500 was added; it was not among the plan's candidates.
3. German RAA 2008 (a plan candidate) was not read: FGSV, paywalled. Its values (lE 250 m including the 60 m taper lZ, for EKA 1 and 2) come from BASt report V277 (2017), which is a secondary source, so the RAA values are marked [VERIFY]. How RAA classes map to 100 km/h was not read.
4. DMRB CD 122 v1.1.1 was read as a primary source.
5. No source indexes guidance by a posted 100 km/h limit, so matching design speeds is approximate. TxDOT rows: 60 and 65 mph. CD 122: the motorway rows have no speed index, and the speed-indexed all-purpose row is '100A kph or less', with the meaning of 'A' not verified against CD 109. Caltrans and RAA are not speed-indexed.
6. Not checked: whether the plant's flows meet the conditional triggers. These are CD 122's 85 %-of-capacity extension, Caltrans' 1,500 veh/h, and TxDOT's 4,600 veh/h. Also not checked: whether the ramp signal is active in E30.

8. Web-search summaries were not used as evidence; only the downloaded documents were.
read.summary:
V5 criterion met: four sources read and recorded. The plant has a 100 km/h limit, 3a_0 and 4a_0 are 294.72 m long, and each is a full-width parallel lane from the ramp junction to an abrupt dead end, with no nose and no taper.

1. **DMRB CD 122 v1.1.1** (primary), Layout B parallel merge. The auxiliary lane runs from the nose tip to the start of the taper, and the taper is not counted. Rural motorway: at least 230 m plus a 75 m taper, or 370 m or more at sustained high flows. Rural all-purpose 100A kph or less: at least 160 m plus 55 m. Reading: inside, meaning above the minimum and below the extended length. Measured to the lane end, the plant is 10 m short of 230 + 75 = 305 m.
2. **TxDOT Roadway Design Manual** (primary; its table likely follows AASHTO [VERIFY]). La is measured from the ramp's controlling point to the start of the taper, and the taper (at least 91 m) is not counted. At 60-65 mph, La runs from 55-113 m (50 mph ramp speed) to 366-430 m (from a stop). The gap-acceptance length is at least 91-152 m. Reading: inside the La span. The plant is above La for ramp speeds of at least 30-40 mph, and below it from a stop and below the 366 m high-volume desirable length.
3. **Caltrans HDM Chapter 500** (primary). On metered entrances, the auxiliary lane beyond the convergence point is at least 91.4 m, or at least 304.8 m above 1,500 veh/h, plus a 183 m taper. Reading: inside, about 10 m below the high-volume minimum.
4. **RAA 2008 via BASt V277** (secondary, [VERIFY]). lE = 250 m, measured from the separating-island tip and including the 60 m taper (EKA 1-2). Reading: above.

Context only: the 295 m sits between the basic minimums and the high-volume or extended lengths. Every source has a 55-183 m end taper, which the plant lacks. checks.citation: National Highways (2022). DMRB CD 122 Geometric design of grade separated junctions, Version 1.1.1, published 31-Jan-2022
checks.corrected_claim: Every extract was found verbatim. Table 3.21 (printed p. 21) gives 'Rural motorway / Mainline 205 1:40 115 230 75 180' and '100A kph or less 130 1:25 75 160 55 150'. NOTE 3 and 3.21.1 are on p. 22, Figure 3.14c on p. 18 and Table 3.5 on p. 14. Figure 3.14c shows Nose | Auxilliary lane | Taper | Entry Datum, so the auxiliary lane runs from the nose tip to the start of the taper, and the taper is not counted. The page numbers and the parallel-merge definition check out. CORRECTION to the judgement: CD 122 gives no range. It gives a 230 m minimum auxiliary lane, plus a 75 m taper, and a separate conditional minimum of 370 m or more that applies only when the 3.21.1 flow condition holds. So the correct reading is: 295 m at full width is ABOVE the 230 m motorway minimum (also above 160 m for all-purpose 100A and 190 m for 120 kph). It is BELOW 370 m only if the 85 %-of-capacity-for-more-than-1,000-h/yr condition holds, and that was not checked. 'Inside' merges two conditional minimums into one range. The plant has no taper, against the 75 m CD 122 requires. Measured from the nose tip to the lane end (entry datum), the plant has 295 m against at least 305 m. The record also leaves out a row: Table 3.21 also indexes urban roads by speed limit. 'Urban road speed limit 60 mph' (about 96.6 km/h) needs at least 125 m plus a 40 m taper, and the plant is above it. So deviation 5's 'no source indexes guidance by a posted limit' is not quite right for CD 122. Table 5.4 also lists 'Rural 100A' as a mainline design speed, which fits 'A' being a CD 109 design-speed band suffix. That is still [VERIFY CD 109].
checks.note: Downloaded again with my own client (4,560,374 bytes, 96 pages; watermark 'CD 122 Version 1.1.1, published: 31-Jan-2022'). I viewed the rendered Figure 3.14c on PDF page 19. The NAA E/1.3 relaxation to 'rural all-purpose 120kph' for existing motorways is real, but it does not change the reading. 'read_in_full: true' overstates what was read: only the definitions, the Section 3 merge clauses and the NAA merge clauses were read, not the whole standard.

checks.corrected_claim: Confirmed verbatim: 15.7.7.1 (the taper is not included in the SCL length; minimum gap-acceptance length 300 ft; use La or Lg, whichever is greater) and 15.7.7.3 (a minimum taper of 300 ft is required; the parallel-lane length is measured from the join to the start of the downstream taper, Lg; part of the ramp may count toward La if the ramp radius is at least 1,000 ft and the view is clear; 1,200 ft plus the taper is desirable near 4,600 veh/h). Table 4-18, row 60: 1200 1140 1100 1020 910 800 550 420 180. Row 65: 1410 1350 1310 1220 1120 1000 770 600 370. Figure 15-25 reads 'La (Measured Along Ramp Alignment)' from Point A, 'Lg (Measured Along Main Lane Alignment)' and '300-Ft Min.' for the taper. 4.10.2.3 gives Lg as 300 to 500 ft depending on nose width. The navigation lists 'Manual Notice 2024-1'. All metric conversions and the 30 mph and 40 mph thresholds are correct. (ii) Stop at the ramp meter: La from a stop is 366-430 m, and the plant's stop line to lane end is about 333 m (rj_0 28.33 + :m_0_0 9.82 + 3a_0 294.72), so the plant is BELOW. (iii) The 366 m desirable length near 4,600 veh/h: the plant is BELOW, but whether that condition applies was not checked. The plant has no taper, against at least 91 m required.

read.summary:
V6 outcome: NOT INFORMATIVE. None of the 7 sources read in full compares SUMO's lane-end (acceleration-lane-end or forced) merging with field data, in particular vehicles stopping or standing at the end of an acceleration lane. Limit M1 stays as written: "the plant's standing at acceleration-lane ends is not validated; the E30 edge sits mostly where it occurs".

What each source compared:
- Erdmann 2014 (SUMO2014 paper) compared the new lane-change model with the old one (JE2013 against DK2008) on waiting time and teleports in three simulated scenarios, arguing realism only qualitatively. It says stopping on a dead lane "does occur in reality as well" without data, and leaves calibration and validation with real-world measurements to future work.
- The Erdmann 2014 slides list "Calibration / Validation using real-world data" as outlook.
- Semrau et al. 2017 analysed lidar field data on 'pushing' merges at Shanghai on-ramps and built SUMO sublane extensions from them. It claims the pushing and merging parameters were compared but shows no simulated-versus-observed numbers.
- Semrau, Erdmann, Friedrich 2018 (EPiC vol 2) is the closest work. It compared SUMO with Chinese driver models and the sublane model against more than 300 Shanghai induction loops (per-lane RMSPE 5-18 %, GEH < 5 at 87 % of detectors). It also compared lane-change safety-factor, lateral-gap and time-gap distributions with test-vehicle data and judged them equal by Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests. It has no lane-end standing measure, and it excluded the one detector at an added lane.
- Semrau et al. 2016 calibrated models from field data and left validation to future work.
- Wiesner et al. 2021 compared a PSO-learned merge model with SUMO's default model in simulation only.
- Veksler et al. 2024/2026 tuned lcAssertive on an I-24 merge by inspection only, with no field data.

Abstract-only and not counted: Berghaus & Oeser 2025 compared a new on-ramp model with two German on-ramps; its abstract does not mention SUMO, and the full text was blocked [VERIFY]. Wang et al. 2023 used AIMSUN, not SUMO. The user-list and GitHub threads describe SUMO lane-end behaviour (vehicles leave an ending lane early, governed by lcStrategic) without field data.

Main caveats: Google Scholar was blocked, and the OpenAlex/WebSearch substitute was screened by title only and partly. The SUMO 2017 proceedings contents and Barthauer 2016 could not be fetched.

verify.outcome_check:
The NOT INFORMATIVE outcome does not hold. Under the rule, INFORMATIVE needs a source read in full that compares SUMO lane-end merging with field data. Kolbe et al. 2023 (arXiv:2308.01093), which I read in full, meets that rule. It ran SUMO with IDM and SUMO's default lane-change model on a replica of the A565 Bonn-Beuel on-ramp and compared it with drone trajectory data. In SUMO, vehicles 'stop and wait for a suitable gap' at the end of the on-ramp lane, which gives large decelerations there; the authors call this 'unrealistic' against the real data. SUMO vehicles also change lanes 'as soon as possible', while real drivers change more towards the end.

The source was found after the fact and outside the fixed terms. Google Scholar was blocked and the substitute screen was by title only, and the title has no 'SUMO'. So the record must label it post hoc.

Suggested V6 wording: "Kolbe et al. (2023) compared SUMO (IDM + default lane-change model) on one German on-ramp against drone trajectories and found simulated vehicles stopping at the on-ramp end with large decelerations, absent in the data [VERIFY version/parameters; one site; graphical]."

Semrau 2018 partly qualifies too: it compares lateral gaps in on-ramp 'pushing' merges with field data, but not lane-end standing.

M1 stays as written, as the plan requires, and this evidence strengthens it. At one field site, SUMO's default lane-end stopping is judged unrealistic, so the E30 edge sitting where standing occurs is a stronger caveat. SUMO's own documentation (Motorways page, 'Motorway ramps' section, which cites no field data) also says simulated vehicles decelerate near the end of an acceleration lane, unlike humans, who 'may accelerate up to the end of the acceleration lane'. It suggests making acceleration lanes 'somewhat longer than in reality'. That statement is worth citing next to M1.

a.other_concerns:
1. Critic-only global inputs (b_env.py:970-973). g0-g2 are zone mean speeds, g3-g5 zone counts /300, g6 the acceleration-lane count /40. g7 is the insertion backlog len(getPendingVehicles())/500, which no sensor can measure. g8 is sim.t/t_end: the simulation clock used as an episode index, i.e. event timing. g9 is flow_ema/(q/3600)/1.5: the demand level q taken from the config. The critic reads them (c_train.py:73, 94-95). The actor never does: in training (c_train.py:207) and at run time (Greedy, c_train.py:128-134) it reads only the 16 local columns. MET therefore holds for the policy's inputs at execution. If a reviewer counts inputs that shape training only through the value baseline, PR-15 would become LIMIT naming g8 and g9. This should be disclosed either way.
2. SUMO range. getLeader and getFollower take dist only as a search bound. SUMO 1.27.1 source (toolchain sumo-src at tag v1_27_1): MSVehicle.cpp:6766-6774 and MSLane.cpp:4441-4451 return the next vehicle on the same lane at any distance, and MSLane.cpp:3142-3151 can return a leader past dist. So columns 6, 7 and 9 can carry information from beyond 100 m or 150 m; columns 5 and 8 saturate and are unaffected. How often this happens is unmeasured. The plant's V2V rule getLeader(v, 150) (b_env.py:788) has the same property; that is outside PR-15 but bears on the V2V-range assumption.
3. Timing. The observation is read at the end of MergeEnv.step (b_env.py:482). The bins are filled at the same sim time (b_env.py:437 -> 851). The action is applied by _apply at the start of the next step (b_env.py:472), before any simulation step. No column is read after the step it is used in. The vv obs_check (vv_merge.py:148-162) only reads.

No observation code reads pert, a lane's max speed, the drawn times, seed, q or t_end; grep over b_env.py:881-980 finds them only in g7-g9. b.other_concerns:
Outcome: MET on PR-15's test. None of the 16 actor columns reads the seed, env.pert (the E30 onset and duration drawn from seed+salt, perturb.py:67-73), any edge or lane speed limit, the demand level q, t_end, or the clock as a scenario index. None reads a future state. Disclosures for the record:

1. Two of the three _obs methods are not v3w's. MergeEnv._obs (327) has the clock as an input (sim.t/t_end, line 360) plus the insertion queue (357-359). ZoneEnv._obs (581) reads the insertion queue (619). Both would fail PR-15, but v3w uses neither.

2. Critic-only global vector (b_env.py:970-973). In training the critic saw the insertion queue (971), the episode clock sim.t/t_end (972) and flow_ema normalised by the configured demand q (973). They go only to Net.value (c_train.py:73, 94-95). The deployed Greedy drops them (c_train.py:129). They shaped training advantages, not deployed inputs. This should be stated so the committee does not mistake it for a leak.

3. Sensing range is not bounded for columns 6, 7 and 9. SUMO 1.27.1 (v5b1 toolchain sumo-src, tag v1_27_1) returns the nearest same-lane leader or follower at any distance: MSVehicle.cpp:6759-6775 and 6785-6792, MSLane.cpp:4440-4456. The docs call getLeader's argument a "minimum look ahead distance" (docs/web/docs/TraCI/Vehicle_Value_Retrieval.md:180). Columns 5 and 8 saturate at 100 m, but 6, 7 and 9 still carry the far vehicle's speed difference and automation flag. So column 7's "V2V within 150 m" is an assumption the code does not enforce. How often it binds was not measured. A read-only count in the smoke or V1 trace would size it: the share of due decisions with a leader or follower beyond 150 m. This is not seed, timing or future state, so MET stands, but the channel statement must say so or carry a limit.

4. Column 14 needs perception of vehicles without V2V on the acceleration lanes, up to ±100 m and across up to three lanes, with no occlusion. It is neither V2V nor a feed the rules read: a stated assumption or a limit.

5. Constants derived from runs or the scenario:
- The running normaliser mean and variance come from training rollouts (C*_config.json: seed0 7,459,320, 520 seeds per worker) and are frozen in each checkpoint. Greedy never calls observe. They do not depend on the evaluated run, scenario or seed.
- The x_remap scale (b_env.py:920-921) and the road starts (913-918) come from the built lane lengths. That is map geometry, fixed per plant variant.

6. self.ramp and self.alks_all come from the seed-generated demand list (b_env.py:166, 409-414). They are read only for the vehicle's own origin (column 2) and the leader's class (column 7).

7. Identity and order: rows follow getIDList order, but the actor is a per-row MLP (c_train.py:41-43, 72, 133). Neither the row index nor the vehicle id is an input. The due mask (966-969) uses each vehicle's own 10-s clock and selects rows; it is not an input.

8. Timing: the observation is built at the end of env.step at time t (b_env.py:482). The action is applied at the start of the next step at the same t (_apply at 472; loop at plant_sweep.py:392-399). Column 12's bins come from the last 1-s sample, with no simulation step in between. Inside a junction, x is the last on-edge value, which is past.

9. Instruments do not touch the policy inputs. vv.obs_check runs after the observation is built (plant_sweep.py:401-402; vv_merge.py:148-162). The read-only check that the v3w input statistics stayed identical is a twin test (V386), outside V7.

10. Scope: inspection only. No runs and no web sources. SUMO behaviour was read from the local 1.27.1 source clone. The checkpoints were read with pickletools and raw tensor bytes, never unpickled.

final.other_concerns:
1. Critic-only globals (b_env.py:970-973). The critic also saw g7, the insertion backlog len(getPendingVehicles())/500, which no sensor measures; g8, sim.t/t_end, an episode clock; and g9, flow_ema/(q/3600)/1.5, which carries the configured demand level q. They enter only Net.value (c_train.py:94-95). The actor never sees them, in training (207, 325) or at execution (Greedy 129-133; actor input 16 in all five checkpoints). Disclose them as privileged training-only inputs. They do not change MET.
2. Sensing range is not enforced for columns 6, 7, 9 or 14. getLeader and getFollower use dist only as a search bound (SUMO 1.27.1 lines in the disagreements; docs/web/docs/TraCI/Vehicle_Value_Retrieval.md:180). Column 7's 'V2V within 150 m' and the on-board ranges are therefore stated assumptions. The plant's own V2V rule (b_env.py:788, getLeader(v, 150)) has the same property. The share of due decisions with a leader or follower beyond 150 m is unmeasured. A read-only count in the smoke or V1 trace would size it.
3. Which rules read the roadside columns. Within the V&V arm set, only LocalRule (lr400_16_1, grid_lr400_13_1) reads a roadside feed: env.bins, the source of column 12. p333 is CavRule at a uniform level 3, and nc reads nothing. Columns 13 and 15 are 'also read by the rules' only through CF-set arms (os*, 3E, ASCH, MPC-F), not through any V&V arm. The channel statement should say which comparison it refers to.
4. Slowdown paths checked. E30 is drawn with default_rng(seed + salt) (perturb.py:67-72) and acts only through ls.edge.setMaxSpeed on edge 2 (perturb.py:185-192). EV has no oracle or hw_oracle key, so oracle_now and hw_now stay None (perturb.py:131-141), and no told or detect switch is attached (plant_sweep.py:127-134). No observation line reads pert, a lane's max speed, the drawn times, the seed, q or t_end; those appear only in g8 and g9. One indirect SUMO path exists. getLeaderOnConsecutive resets its search bound from the next lane's current max speed (MSLane.cpp:3154-3155), and E30 sets that speed on edge 2. On r2m3 this path cannot change any result: it acts only after a whole empty next lane, and edge 2 is about 498 m (ROAD_X, b_env.py:87), longer than any bound, so the loop stops (MSLane.cpp:3157, 3161). It is also present-state information, a posted limit, not event timing.
5. Timing. The observation is built at the end of MergeEnv.step (482), after the last 1-s sample, whose bins are filled at the same sim time (436-437 -> 851). The action from it is applied at the start of the next step (472), before any SUMO step. The instruments wrapped around _sim_step and _second (plant_sweep.py:141-370), vv_merge.py and measure.py contain no SUMO set, subscribe or env-state writes. obs_check (vv_merge.py:148-163) only reads. policy_probs is a pure function (measure.py:42-56). Every run uses measure (c1.arm_cfg sets it), and measure never calls env._x.
6. Identity and order. No column holds a vehicle id. The actor is a per-row MLP (c_train.py:41-42, 88-89). due (966-969) is a per-vehicle 10-s clock that selects rows; it is not an input. alks_all and ramp come from the seed-generated demand list but are read only for own origin (column 2) and the leader's class (column 7).
7. Normalisation. lo_mean and lo_var are frozen in each checkpoint from training rollouts (n_seen as above). Greedy never calls observe. Training seeds 7,464,000-7,471,799 do not overlap the V&V seeds 7,489,160-7,493,010.
8. Scope. I inspected the run code at 6e96988 and the five checkpoints, plus a partial git-history check of CavEnv._obs and the observation helpers in b_env.py from d2b2ecc to 6e96988. I did not establish the training commit. No runs, no web sources. SUMO behaviour comes from the local clone at tag v1_27_1.
